title: Small molecule inhibitors of Slit2/Robo signaling as novel therapeutics for glioblastoma
text:
There is an unmet need to develop innovative immunomodulatory strategies to overcome immune
suppression in glioblastoma. The focus of this work is to validate a new therapeutic strategy for glioblastoma
based on a novel macrophage-based immunotherapy approach. SLIT2/ROBO inhibitors from this work will
represent promising candidates for future evaluation in preclinical models of glioblastoma.

title: Role of Long Non-Coding RNAs in Exosome Biogenesis
text:
Exosomes are nano-sized vesicles produced by all cells in both physiological and pathological states that play
a vital role in multiple biological processes including cell-cell communication, immune regulation, tissue
development and regeneration, and cancer metastasis. Exosomes represent excellent candidates for the
development of new diagnostic and therapeutic tools, yet the mechanism controlling their biogenesis is poorly
understood. In this Project, we will study the role of long non-coding RNA (a novel class of gene expression
regulators) on exosome biogenesis, thereby advancing our understanding of these mechanisms and providing
the basis for the use of exosomes as novel biomarkers and the development of new therapeutics.

title: Integrated, Multidisciplinary Training in Cardiovascular Research
text:
This training grant, which is in its 45th year, provides NIH funds to the Cardiology Division at the Massachusetts
General Hospital to train the next generation of scientists in cardiovascular research. Our training program
continues to have an excellent track record of training scientists who remain in academia/research and go on to
become leaders in their chosen research fields.

title: High throughput electrosynthesis for enhanced drug discovery via light-powered smart microelectronics
text:
The development of disruptive synthetic technologies to rapidly access drug molecules is a pressing priority in
today’s pharmaceutical industry. Researchers face increasing challenges in creating new treatments, leaving
millions of patients reliant on suboptimal medications or without effective options. OWiC Technologies’ innovative
solution provides drug developers with new synthetic tools to expand compound libraries with molecules
previously unattainable through conventional methods, accelerating drug discovery to address unmet medical
needs in conditions such as heart disease, cancer, and diabetes.

title: Core B: Bioinformatics and Immunology Core
text:
The three RPs proposed in this P01 aim to study how novel polymer-based glioblastoma (GBM) vaccine (RP1),
in vivo generation of CAR-T using a novel biomaterial (RP2), novel CAR-NKT therapy (RP3), and their
combinations can benefit GBM treatment in various pre-clinical GMB animal models (Core C). Core B is to (1)
identify the functionally meaningful cellular, molecular, genetic, and epigenetic changes of the immune system
during GBM development in various models (Core C) and treatment (RPs) and (2) to assist the RPs in
understanding the underlying mechanisms. Core B will support the RPs to test the hypothesis that the novel
approaches employed will induce effective and lasting anti-GBM immunity, through enriched specificities towards
tumor antigens, by co-opting endogenous and transferred immune cells.

title: Tools to determine and analyze the structures of molecular machines in motion
text:
The conformation and composition of massive molecular machines change as they are
assembled and as they perform their essential cellular functions. Work proposed here will produce
broadly impactful computational tools to determine the structures of these dynamic machines in
motion. Such structures are critical in furthering our understanding of how these molecules
function in healthy cells and how they fail in times of disease, and in guiding the development of
therapeutics treating a wide array of human illnesses.

title: Examining precursors to language impairment in ASD via remote assessment
text:
This project will establish robust tasks for assessing mechanisms related to language impairment in autism
during infancy, before a clinical diagnosis can be made. This work extends recent efforts in our group to establish
a remote and scalable battery of tasks for the assessment of cognitive development in this population. Valid and
robust measures of cognitive and language development that are scalable to large populations of infants will
allow us to gather the critical information we need for future development of targeted interventions in a population
as heterogeneous as children with autism.

title: Linking Impulsivity Domains and Subjective Response to Alcohol in Young Adults Using Lab and Daily Assessment Methods
text:
Findings from this project will determine the relationship between two vulnerability factors for Alcohol Use
Disorder (AUD) in young adults: impulsivity and subjective response to alcohol. The results will identify badly
needed, novel targets for prevention and treatment efforts to simultaneously reduce impulsivity and subjective
responses in at-risk young adults. As such, the project is directly relevant to NIAAA’s mission to identify
mechanisms of alcohol action and facilitate prevention and treatment research.

title: Atypical astrocytes in aging and Alzheimer's Disease
text:
NARRATIVE.
Astrocytes contribute to neuronal activity, blood-brain-barrier function, inflammatory response, and more, but
how astrocytes change during aging and in age-related neurological disorders is not well understood. Here we
report a novel astrocyte phenotype in normal aging, that is exacerbated in the APPNL-G-F mouse model of
Alzheimer’s Disease (AD), known as “atypical astrocytes” (AtAs) in which astrocytes lose multiple functional
proteins but do not appear to be reactive. In this proposal we will determine the molecular characteristics of AtA,
their functional consequences, and the role of vascular dysfunction in driving AtA formation during healthy aging
and in a mouse model of AD.

title: Translating genomic discoveries to improved outcomes for high risk acute leukemia
text:
(RELEVANCE STATEMENT)
Acute leukemia (ALL) is the commonest childhood tumor and a leading cause of cancer death in the young. My
research has used integrated genomic discovery, experimental modeling and therapeutic development to identify
and characterize the genomic drivers of disease and develop new treatment approaches. My proposed research
program will build upon my prior discoveries to pursue several new conceptually and technically innovative areas
central to advancing cure rates for these diseases, including the mechanistic basis of enhancer deregulation in
leukemia, the role of BCL11B in lineage ambiguous leukemia, the mechanistic role and potential for therapeutic
targeting of LMO2/STAG2 alterations in leukemia, the role of liquid-liquid phase separation mediated by fusion
oncoproteins in leukemia, and their potential for therapeutic targeting. I will also develop innovative protein
degradation approaches using molecular glues to degrade hitherto intractable cancer drivers of high-risk
leukemia.

title: Mechanisms, regulation, and cell biology of rare CRISPR-Cas9 immunization events
text:
Phages, the natural predators of bacteria, represent a promising weapon against the growing threat of
antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Our research aims to understand how bacteria survive new phage threats using
the CRISPR-Cas9 adaptive immune system. Our findings will inform the development of therapeutic phages
that ward off phage-resistance, and our studies of Cas9 in its native host could yield new insights into Cas9-
based technologies.

title: IP24-045, SEAPREP:  Seattle Pandemic Preparedness Cohort
text:
Respiratory viruses, like SARS-CoV-2 and RSV, can cause major problems in society by making people sick
and causing death, especially in older people, babies, and those with weakened immune systems. The
proposed work will provide critical information on who these viruses affect, how quickly they spread in
communities and in households, and how well we are protected by vaccines and previous infections. This
information will better inform how to protect people from getting sick, and allow us to respond quickly and
effectively to new outbreaks.

title: A Revitalized Framework for Vitamin Biology: New Sensors, Pathways and Precision Therapies
text:
Our proposed research seeks to revitalize the field of vitamin biology using modern approaches. We aim to
identify all enzymes and metabolic pathways dependent on vitamins, discover new vitamin sensors that regulate
essential biological processes, and pinpoint genetic diseases that can be treated with megavitamin therapies.
By leveraging modern techniques, we hope to revive and expand the understanding of vitamin metabolism,
leading to personalized vitamin-based treatments and potentially instant cures for numerous genetic disorders.

title: High-throughput snapshot hyperspectral imager for multiplexed fluorescence microscopy
text:
This project will develop a snapshot hyperspectral imager compatible with widefield microscopy.
By enabling faster, multiplexed fluorophore imaging with reduced phototoxicity, the technology
will improve the research community’s ability to study complex biological systems and discover
new biomarkers.
In the long term, the ability to observe spectral and spatial information in tissue simultaneously
will advance all imaging-based precision medicine and translational research.

title: Enhancing TIL efficacy in NSCLC through epigenetic reprogramming and computational modeling
text:
The short-term goal of this K99/R00 application is to develop the PI as an independent investigator, skilled in
cancer informatics, tumor immunology, and modern experimental science; the long-term goal is to enhance
tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) therapy in lung cancer patients. The proposed research will test the efficacy
of epigenetic modulation paired TILs in lung cancer through in vivo and in vitro studies with de-identified human
samples. The project will also use modern sequencing data and methods from mathematical biology to discover
mechanisms of T cell suppression, and suggest novel targets for TIL-combination treatment.

title: Disease pathways in the population determined by amyloid, tau, and neurodegeneration imaging biomarkers
text:
The current cycle of AG011378 was designed to test aspects of a hypothetical model of the temporal
evolution of Alzheimer’s biomarkers that we proposed; however, a major missing element when the current
cycle of AG011378 began was a method to measure fibrillar tau deposits with imaging. Tau PET has recently
become available and consequently for the first time imaging biomarkers exist to ascertain three of the most
important pathologic features of AD: amyloid, tau and neurodegeneration. Our aims in this renewal application
are to empirically evaluate our hypothetical model of AD biomarkers and to create new imaging biomarker
models for individuals who are not in the Alzheimer’s continuum using imaging measures of amyloid, tau, and
neurodegeneration.

title: Genome-wide Analysis and Enrichment of Chimeric DNA Fragments in Plasma for Early Detection of Cancer
text:
Cancer is the second leading cause of death, and earlier detection leads to better survival outcomes. While
promising, recent advances in plasma DNA blood tests do not yet achieve adequate diagnostic accuracy to be
widely useful for early cancer detection. This project seeks to study a ubiquitous, but under-utilized, class of
genomic changes in cancer DNA called structural variants to develop an accurate cancer detection blood test
based on whole genome sequencing of plasma DNA.

title: TOWARD TRANSLATION OF NANFORMULATED PACLITAXEL-PLATINUM COMBINATION
text:
The goal of this proposal is to obtain pre-clinical data to enable the translation of a novel nanotechnology-based
immunotherapeutic drug to treat triple negative breast cancer that is currently associated with poor prognosis.
We use nanotechnology for combination therapy with two drugs in the same nanoparticle allowing drugs to attack
cancer cells in a collaborative fashion and produce greater antitumor effect. We will develop validated procedures
for manufacturing and analysis of the combination therapeutic and assess its safety, delivery to tumors and
efficacy in comparison with the standard therapeutics in animal models that recapitulate human disease.

title: Impact of Exercise Adaptations on the Aging Stem Cell
text:
This project will significantly contribute to our understanding of how exercise interventions impact stem cell
aging. By using a multidisciplinary approach, we will uncover the key molecular complement and gene
regulatory signatures affected by a conserved cell signaling pathway known for its role to mediate inflammatory
responses. Determining how exercise modulates this pathway to render the purported benefits for aging stem
cells is critically important for devising intervention strategies to combat aging-induced stem cell impairment.

title: Dysregulation of the opioid system in early life adversity
text:
We propose that abnormal dysregulation of the brain beta-endorphin signaling pathway plays a central role
linking insecure attachment with key behavioral and cognitive hallmarks of childhood maltreatment. We plan to
test this novel idea using a mouse model of complex trauma combined with new tools to record and manipulate
specific populations of neurons in the mouse brain. At its conclusion, this work will illuminate novel targets that
can reduce the devastating psychiatric and medical consequences of childhood maltreatment.
